comprehension.C1: A hash table with chaining gives O(1) lookup by key. A doubly linked list tracks recency so the LRU victim at the tail is found and removed in O(1). Each entry is in both a hash chain and the recency list at the same time (intrusive links).
comprehension.C2: It copies the value, allocates an entry, inserts it into the bucket and at the list head, increments count and bytes_used, then a loop evicts from the tail until both the count and byte limits are satisfied. The eviction callback is invoked for each victim.
comprehension.C3: pp points at the link that points to the current node: either the bucket slot or the previous node's hash_next. Unlinking is just *pp = e->hash_next, with no special case for the head of the chain.
comprehension.C4: put copies the value in and get copies it out, so the caller never holds a pointer into the cache. The cache frees its copies on delete, evict, expire and destroy. The key is copied into a fixed-size inline array.

bugs.explanation: entry_free(victim) runs before the callback, so the callback gets the freed key and value: use after free, victim used after free, dangling pointer.
bugs.fix: Invoke the callback first, then free the entry.

bugs.explanation: drop_expired frees e, then the loop increment reads e->prev from freed memory: use after free of the loop iterator.
bugs.fix: Save prev = e->prev before calling drop_expired.

bugs.explanation: The expiry path never decrements bytes_used, so accounting drifts upward and the eviction loop can spin forever.
bugs.fix: Subtract value_len from bytes_used in drop_expired.

bugs.explanation: Key length off by one: a 64-char key passes the check and strncpy leaves it unterminated.
If the bucket calloc fails the function returns NULL without freeing c: leak of the cache struct.

design.D1: Every get mutates the recency list, so a read-write lock does not help. Shard the cache by hash into N independent caches with their own locks, or use approximate LRU (CLOCK) to avoid a list update on every hit. Measure contention before optimizing.
design.D2: Re-entrancy deadlock if the callback calls lru_* because the mutex is non-recursive, and a slow callback blocks all threads. Collect victims and invoke callbacks after unlocking, and document callback restrictions.

improvements.title: Factor one remove_entry() helper
improvements.detail: Used by delete, evict and expire to keep accounting in one place.

improvements.title: Add tests
improvements.detail: Sanitizers (ASan, UBSan, TSan), Valgrind, and a stress test with invariant checks on count and bytes_used.
